title: How to Write the Common App Activities Section (Koppelman Group)
text: Practical guide to the Common App Activities section. It's short but high-leverage: with grades and scores off the table here, this is where you show you're driven and engaged. Reference for building runchen robotics competition journey, runchen soccer and school clubs, runchen music activities etc. into a coherent list; pairs with the expanded resume in runchen resume review and improvement suggestions aug 2026 and the trait signals in applicant characteristics each college expects fall 2027 cycle. The format Up to 10 activities, each with: activity type (dropdown), role/position, organization name, a 150-character description, years of involvement + timing within the year, hours per week and weeks per year, and whether you'll continue it in college. "Activity" is broad — school clubs, national orgs, jobs, neighborhood, or family responsibilities all count. Choosing what to list Quality over quantity. Fewer than 10 is fine; padding with filler hurts you — low reported hours expose throwaway entries. List in order of importance to you — activities that shaped you as a person and a student. text: Companion to runchen-college-list-draft-2026 and runchen-college-essay-requirements-master-list-fall-2027-cycle: for every school on the list, what the institution says it weighs most, and separately what the engineering school specifically requires or values. Researched 2026-07-25 for Runchen's Fall-2027 cycle. How to read this Two kinds of evidence, and they are not equally reliable: Common Data Set section C7 — the authoritative one. Every college self-reports each factor as Very Important / Important / Considered / Not Considered. It is a ranked, comparable, audited-ish disclosure, not marketing. Section C8A gives the testing policy; C5 gives required high-school units. Where C7 is quoted below it is verbatim from the school's own CDS. "What we look for" prose — useful for tone and for engineering-specific requirements, but every school says it wants curious, rigorous, community-minded students. Treat prose as tiebreak color, C7 as the actual weighting. C7 covers general admission — it explicitly excludes "programs with specific criteria." That is exactly why the engineering-school sections below matter: at CMU, Cornell, Cal Poly, and Georgia Tech the engineering rules override the C7 table. One thing C7 cannot tell you: it says character/personal qualities is "Very Important" at six of his hardest schools, but not which qualities. That question is answered separately in applicant-characteristics-each-college-expects-fall-2027-cycle — where only MIT, Cornell, Olin, and CMU turn out to publish an explicit named trait list. title: Worcester Polytechnic Institute — College Research
text: Worcester Polytechnic Institute (WPI) — Worcester, MA (~1 hour from Greater Boston). Known for its robotics program; a potential target school. Part of the runchen-college-counseling-working-school-list-student-profile; see also runchen-wu-college-application-profile, runchen-robotics-competition-journey, and runchen-college-preferences-overall. Links: Bachelor's in Robotics Engineering (wpi.edu/academics/study/robotics-engineering-bs); The WPI Plan (project-based learning). Likes (parents) Robotics major; well known in the robotics community/industry. The only ABET-accredited Robotics Engineering BS in the country with a dedicated department, dedicated labs, and a robotics-specific curriculum (not bolted onto ME/ECE). Has Early Action (EA) — could be a good target. Less burdensome Common App supplement. 4+1 / BS/MS Plan. Concerns (parents) Less national brand prestige. The 7-week-term Plan is intense and unusual. Smaller social scene. Runchen's Own Take Likes: strong focus on engineering and project-based learning; the famous "WPI Plan" emphasizes real-world, hands-on problem solving; dedicated Robotics Engineering degree (he sees it as relevant to AI + human-tech future fields); good preparation for industry jobs straight out of undergrad; Worcester is more industrial/quiet than Boston. Dislikes: less theoretical depth than some research-heavy schools. Worry: "Does it feel awkward?" — concern about the smaller social scene and fitting in socially (see runchen-college-preferences-overall). Open Questions Is WPI a good school to attend?
